title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description:
You are given an array of k linked lists, each linked list is sorted in ascending order.

Merge all the linked lists into one sorted linked list and return its head.

If N is the total number of nodes across all lists, aim for a solution that scales well as k grows (better than merging one list at a time).

examples.explanation: The linked lists are [1,4,5], [1,3,4], and [2,6]. Merging them into one sorted list gives 1->1->2->3->4->4->5->6.

constraints: lists[i] is sorted in ascending order.
The sum of lists[i].length will not exceed 10^4.

approach: Treat merging k lists as repeatedly combining pairs. A min-heap holds the current front node of each nonempty list keyed by value; popping the smallest and pushing its successor emits the next output node in O(log k) per step, giving O(N log k) overall with O(k) auxiliary space. An equivalent divide-and-conquer approach merges lists in pairs (interval doubling), halving the list count each round for the same O(N log k) time. Both reuse the existing nodes, so only O(1) extra list storage is needed beyond the heap or recursion bookkeeping.
